From: Megan Torres <megan@healthlytics.com>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval MAP + what success looks like

Hi Monica,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — team was impressed by the runtime and the cost controls. We have a four-week evaluation window the product team has carved out and need a clear mutual action plan so we can: (1) validate latency and cost at expected load, (2) prove fidelity on our clinical extraction prompts, and (3) capture observability/evidence for our security/compliance review.

Can you send a short MAP that spells out acceptance tests, hard stop exit gates, and suggested timelines (we're aiming to decide by the end of Week 5)? Also include what evidence you need from our side (sample data, test harness, SSO details).

Cheers,
Megan

Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval MAP + what success looks like

Hi Megan — great to connect. Attached is a draft MAP and a companion acceptance-test workbook that maps each success criterion to concrete tests and owners. High level summary below; full detail in the attachments (redwood-map-draft-v1.pdf, healthlytics-acceptance-tests-v1.xlsx).

Proposed timeline (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (kickoff): onboarding, SSO + data access, baseline perf snapshot
- Week 1: smoke tests + latency load ramp (10k qps bursts simulated), KV/prefix caching baseline
- Week 2: fidelity probes vs. 250 clinical prompts; sample-size 1k prompts across 3 modalities
- Week 3: long-run cost sampling (24h steady-state), and reliability/rollback drills
- Week 4: compile evidence pack, run acceptance checklist, exec review; sign-off or close

Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 220ms for standard prompt slice, p99 <= 480ms for long context tests
- Cost target: avg token cost within 15% of benchmarked threshold
- Fidelity: >= 92% match on structured extraction (as measured by Healthlytics label set)
- Reliability: <0.1% error rate; graceful fallback to smaller model variant on overload

Exit gates (hard stops):
- Any fidelity drop below 86% after remediation attempts
- Sustained p99 > 800ms under target load
- Unresolved security evidence requests (SOC2 artifacts, KMS proof) after 5 business days

Acceptance tests (examples):
- Smoke: 20 canonical prompts run against canary + baseline environment (pass/fail)
- Load: ramp to expected QPS (scripts included) and confirm SLOs over 1h window
- Regression: run historical failure-case suite (50 vignettes) and measure concordance
- Audit: confirm access logs, KMS key rotation evidence, and data retention config

What we need from Healthlytics:
- A representative prompt set (CSV) and 100 labeled examples for fidelity baseline
- List of entitlement users + SSO metadata (SAML)
- Confirmation of any regulatory redlines (DPA clauses) you want validated during the run

Next steps: if this looks good we'll: (a) lock timeline and test owners, (b) provision a dedicated canary pool for Week 1, and (c) share the DocuSign for the MAP so legal can sign.

Thanks — looping in Aditya for the smoke test artifacts and Sean for commercial/SLA notes.

Best,
Monica Patel

Thanks — quick technical notes:
- For the load profile you described, we'll start with the provided QPS script (attached redwood-smoke-tests.yml). It simulates your expected burst patterns and background traffic.
- Smoke test pass criteria: 0 dropped requests, <0.05% token decode errors, and KV cache hit >= 78% for repeated prefixes.
- Fidelity probes: recommend stratifying prompts by intent buckets (diagnosis, medication extraction, triage). Aditya to own the probe harness; Monica to coordinate data ingestion.

I'll also include an automated checklist that writes evidence artifacts (trace IDs, token-level latency histograms) to the shared drive for your compliance team.
